ruling: R47 (Drew, 2026-09-15): Allen & Ginter MINIS are their own card set.
status: NO PACKAGE BUILT — the measurement contradicts the premise the ruling was given on. Reported for Drew rather than built.
scope: baseball/2025/topps-allen-ginter (1,938 mini rows; 2023 and 2024 are 153 and 71 rows, both under the 500-row bar)
whatIWasAskedToBuild: Register `topps-allen-ginter-mini` as its own card set with its own ladder from the stated source, plus a re-key list for pool rows naming a mini.
whyItWasNotBuilt: THE MINIS ARE ALREADY CHECKLIST-BACKED, AS RUNGS. baseball/2025/topps-allen-ginter holds 40 distinct mini-named rungs from checklist sources — `Mini`, `Minis`, `Mini Wood`, `Mini Glossy`, `Mini No Number`, `Mini Brooklyn Back`, `Mini M&N Back`, `Framed Mini Printing Plates` and more, most at 350 cards each. Nothing is missing to acquire.

AND THE MINIS REPRINT THE BASE ROSTER, so they are not separately numbered. The partition test, run against the catalog's own rows: of the 350 numeric cards on the plain `Mini` rung, 349 name the SAME player the base print names at that number. The single difference is #327 `Vladimir Guerrero` vs `Vladimir Guerrero Sr.` — the same person. (25 further rows differ only by an `RC` suffix and were folded before this count.) A card set with its own numbering would not reprint another set's roster 349 times out of 350.

SO A SEPARATE `topps-allen-ginter-mini` KEY WOULD SPLIT ONE POOL IN TWO. The mini and the base card share a number and a player; moving the minis to their own key would put the same card at two addresses, which is the `one card, one row, one pool` invariant failing on a new axis.

whatTheRealDefectIs.summary: A SPELLING problem, not an acquisition. 1,211 of the 1,938 mini pool rows already sit on a rung the catalog spells the same way. The other 726 sit on a rung the catalog spells differently.

unbackedRungsAndTheirBackedCounterparts.note: no candidate — the only genuinely unbacked rung of any size

whatTheRealDefectIs.note: Several counterparts are AMBIGUOUS — `red-refractor` could be the Mini Cards Chrome rung or the Chrome Variations rung, and those are different cards. That ambiguity is exactly what the exactly-one rule in checklistSpellingAdoption.ts refuses to resolve, and it is not resolvable from the pool text alone.

questionsForDrew: R47 was ruled on the premise that A&G minis are their own card set. The catalog says they are a RUNG of the base print that reprints its roster 349/350. Does R47 still stand, or do minis stay a rung? (If they stay a rung, nothing needs building and the 726 rows are a vocabulary job.)

If minis DO become their own card set, the 40 existing mini rungs on `topps-allen-ginter` have to move too — otherwise the same card sits on both keys. That is a catalog relocation, not an acquisition, and it is much larger than the 1,938 pool rows. Authorise separately?
`image-variation` (17 rows) has no backed counterpart at all and is the one real gap here. Acquire the A&G image-variation list, or leave 17 rows unbacked?

measurement.note: pool read by slug prefix and paged; catalog read per (sport, year, setKey); no cross-partition COUNT over sold_comps.
